ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure, with the main body being a six-membered carbon ring, and two C=C double bonds drawn inside the ring; an carbonyl oxygen is connected to the upper left of the ring, shown as C=O; on the right side of the ring there is a substituent, where the ring carbon is connected to a CCl2 carbon, and this carbon is further connected to two Cl. In the figure, an H, a negative charge mark, and several curved arrows can also be seen. Reasoning count: Count according to the number of connections, and do not additionally count the second parallel line of a double bond as another bond. The six-membered ring has a total of 6 C-C connections; the carbonyl C=O on the upper left is counted as 1 bond; in the substituent on the right side, the ring carbon to the CCl2 carbon is counted as 1 bond, and the CCl2 carbon to the two Cl are each counted as 1 bond, giving a total of 2 C-Cl bonds. The visible C-H bond is not counted, and curved arrows and charge marks are not counted. Therefore the total is 6 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 10.

method.method_draft: First describe the image contents, then count by parts. Count the six C-C connections making up the six-membered ring, treating the two drawn double bonds as bonds but not counting the extra parallel line separately. Add the carbonyl C=O bond at the top-left ring atom. Add the substituent bonds on the right: the ring carbon to the CCl2 carbon, and the two C-Cl bonds. Exclude the visible C-H bond and all curved arrows/charge marks. Sum 6 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 10.

method.method_draft: First describe the image, then build the heavy-atom adjacency list. Around the ring, list the six unique adjacent C-C pairs. Add the O--carbonyl carbon pair.
